newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Daim says stocks low enough to buy.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Daim says stocks low enough to buy.

text.p: Malaysia's Government Economic Advisor Daim Zainuddin said on Thursday that current low stock market prices present a buying opportunity.
"The market is so low it is an opportunity to buy," he told reporters at a fund management conference.

The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's key Composite Index opened weaker, to extend Wednesday's 2.32 percent plunge on concerns over possible firm domestic interest rates to protect the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Around 0155 GMT, the index was down 6.78 points or 0.66 percent to 1,026.46, off from an earlier low of 1,018.43.
Daim said: "It is a time for you to buy".
He said the economy and the corporate sector were both performing well.
"Companies are doing very well...and the eight percent (economic growth target) will be met," the economic advisor said.
"These days what happens outside the country also affects the country," he said.
The Kuala Lumpur market has been recently hit by spillover effects from the Thai baht crisis and clashes in Cambodian.
When asked why local investors were also shying away if the current stock market slump was only an international perception problem, Daim said: "I've been saying this is not really a matured market."
He said investors should not base their trading on stock market rumours.
